title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 121
paragraphs: Meanwhile the Greeks, when it proved that they were unable to take Andros, turned to Carystos, and having laid waste the land of that people they departed and went to Salamis. First, for the gods they set aside first-fruits of the spoils, including three Persian triremes — one to be dedicated at the Isthmus, which was still there in my time; another at Sunion; and the third to Ajax at Salamis, where they were. After this they divided the rest of the spoils among themselves and sent the first-fruits to Delphi, from which was made a statue holding in its hand the beak of a ship and measuring twelve cubits in height. This statue stood in the same place as the golden statue of Alexander the Macedonian.
